To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for a two-dimensional shear flow in a channel of aspect ratio α, the number of degrees of freedom is bounded above by cαRe32, where c is a constant that depends only on the geometry and the kinematic viscosity.

the degrees of freedom in a two-dimensional channel flow are bounded by the Reynolds number cubed times a constant that is independent of the Reynolds number, but depends on the geometry of the domain, the type of forcing and the type of boundary conditions.

the degrees of freedom for the large time behavior in a two-dimensional channel flow with aspect ratio α and Reynolds number Re is bounded from above by cα Re 2.5, where c is a positive universal constant, for both the boundary and pressure gradient driven cases, and that this upper bound is sharp in the sense that it can be achieved by a shear flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large-time behavior of the solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes system in two-dimensional channels.
the large time behavior and dimensionality of solutions of the Naviers-Stokes equations in elongated two- dimensional channels.

the large time behavior and the degrees of freedom, or the dimension of the global attractor, of solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation for fluid flows in elongation two-dimensional channels with different types of driving mechanisms.

the degrees of freedom for a given flow are proportional to a universal positive constant times the Reynolds number to the 3/2 power, times the aspect ratio of a channel to the power 1/2.

the dimension of the global attractor for the Navier-Stoke equations for two-dimensional channel flows is bounded above by the Reynolds number to a power between 3/2 and 2.
